coverage.finding: Reviewed 2026-10-01: Fabru HDPE GF20 originals (G138-01/G138-02) discuss generic polyethylene behaviour and explicitly describe difficulty painting or gluing. These are incomplete finishing limitations and polymer context, without a demonstrated product-specific finishing method or application qualification. Physiologically harmless wording about PE is not printed-product safety evidence. G138-03 iSANMATE is outside this maker batch and remains individually unassessed. Reviewed source basis: R-FABRU-PUREFIL-3493-Materialdatenblatt-HDPE-GF20-purefil, R-FABRU-3492-Material-data-sheet-HDPE-GF20-purefil.
Canonical identity recorded: Polyethylene (Glass fibre) (Polyolefins, base polymer PE). Aliases and disputed entries are family entries of their own.
H2C status "Theoretical" is recorded with no document cited behind it.
7 mechanical measurement(s) of this material's own grades. See specimen, direction, moisture, preparation and standard before comparing.
3 thermal measurement(s) of this material's own grades. HDT, Tg and Vicat are not continuous-service ratings.
3 print profile(s) publishing a nozzle, bed, chamber or drying setting: P1446, P1455, P1465. Check other setup fields individually.

2 exposure, solubility or moisture record(s) from this material's own sources, all of them its makers' statements on moisture sensitivity (drying, storage, water uptake). Test conditions are rarely stated; not a chemical database.

polymer.basis: Classification and typical values from polymer handbooks and resin data sheets, as compiled for the estimate model (docs/audits/2026-09-15-filtering-estimates-data/physics/). The document cited prints a density inside the range, not its ends. Mitsubishi Chemical Advanced Materials' sheet for Proteus HDPE (R-MCAM-PROTEUS-HDPE-DS), a high-density polyethylene, prints a specific gravity of 0.96 (ASTM D792; its ISO density cell is empty) and a water absorption in water at 23 °C below 0.01 % after 24 h and below 0.01 % at saturation (ISO 62 and ASTM D570), p. 1. The Cambridge Materials Data Book (R-CUED-MATERIALS-DATA-BOOK-2003, SHA-256 2bcf739fd66f...) gives polyethylene 0.939-0.96 Mg/m³. Neither prints a figure below 0.939, where the range begins at 0.900.
